01/Research

Randomness, geometry and markets

My research sits where probability meets analysis. Stochastic analysis provides a language for systems that evolve randomly in time; optimal transport provides a geometry for comparing probability distributions. Mathematical finance and machine learning supply many of the questions that motivate the work.

  1. i. dXt

    Stochastic Analysis

    The calculus of randomness: how to describe, and compute with, quantities that change unpredictably over time.

    In technical terms Stochastic differential equations, semimartingale theory and stochastic calculus on infinite-dimensional spaces.

  2. ii. W2(μ, ν)

    Optimal Transport

    The most efficient way to move one distribution of mass onto another, which gives a natural way of measuring the distance between probability distributions.

    In technical terms Wasserstein geometry, martingale optimal transport and connections to partial differential equations.

  3. iii. 𝔼ℚ[ · ]

    Mathematical Finance

    How to price and hedge financial contracts robustly: when the model itself is uncertain, when buying and selling prices differ, and when markets contain very many assets.

    In technical terms Model-independent pricing, conic finance and large financial markets.

  4. iv. ∇θ ℒ

    Mathematical Machine Learning

    Using the same tools to understand when and why learning algorithms work.

    In technical terms Applications of stochastic analysis and optimal transport to learning theory.

05/Notes & Learning Resources

A library of study notes

Study notes on core topics in mathematics, statistics and computing, compiled while learning and teaching. Most sets build from definitions to the main theorems, with figures, common pitfalls and references for further reading.

Please note. These are personal notes compiled for reference and learning. They may contain errors, incomplete information or personal interpretations, and they are not peer-reviewed. For academic or professional purposes, please consult textbooks, research papers or other authoritative sources.

Foundations of mathematics

The core of an undergraduate mathematics degree.

Mathematical Analysis 3

  • Sequences and Series Completeness, Bolzano–Weierstrass, Cauchy sequences, convergence tests, power series. Updated August 2026
  • Continuity and Limits Limits, the Intermediate and Extreme Value Theorems, uniform continuity. Updated August 2026
  • Convergence Theory Pointwise and uniform convergence, interchanging limits, the Weierstrass M-test. Updated August 2026

Calculus 3

  • Differentiation The chain rule, the Mean Value Theorem, L’Hôpital’s rule, Taylor’s theorem. Updated August 2026
  • Integration Riemann sums, the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, improper and numerical integration. Updated August 2026
  • Multivariable Calculus Gradients, the Hessian, the Implicit Function Theorem, Lagrange multipliers. Updated August 2026

Linear Algebra 3

  • Matrices and Operations Matrix multiplication, determinants, invertibility, rank, Gaussian elimination. Updated August 2026
  • Vector Spaces Bases and dimension, rank–nullity, inner products, orthogonal projection, Gram–Schmidt. Updated August 2026
  • Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors Diagonalisation, the spectral theorem, the power method, PCA. Updated August 2026

Discrete Mathematics 3

  • Combinatorics Inclusion–exclusion, generating functions, Catalan numbers, Ramsey theory. Updated August 2026
  • Graph Theory Trees, planarity and Euler’s formula, colouring, matchings and Hall’s theorem. Updated August 2026
  • Mathematical Logic Propositional logic, soundness and completeness, compactness, resolution. Updated August 2026

Number Theory 3

  • Prime Numbers The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, the Prime Number Theorem, primality tests. Updated December 2024
  • Modular Arithmetic Congruences, modular inverses, Euler’s theorem, the Chinese Remainder Theorem. Updated December 2024
  • Cryptography RSA, Diffie–Hellman, elliptic-curve cryptography, digital signatures. Updated December 2024

Statistics, econometrics & learning

Econometrics 4

Machine Learning 3

06/Science Communication & Outreach

Beyond the seminar room

Mathematics, AI and scientific research are also about education, collaboration and community. Alongside research, I help build initiatives that bring students into contact with these fields.

  1. ONIA↗ (opens in a new tab)

    Co-founder · Organising Committee

    Olimpíadas Nacionais de Inteligência Artificial · Portuguese Olympiads in Artificial Intelligence

    The national olympiad in artificial intelligence for students from the 7th to the 12th grade in Portugal. It combines a classroom challenge that requires no programming with an olympiad track that selects the team representing Portugal at the International Olympiad in Artificial Intelligence (IOAI).

  2. Gradient

    Co-founder

    Co-organiser of the Portuguese Olympiads in Artificial Intelligence, together with TreeTree2.

  3. JunctionX Lisbon↗ (opens in a new tab)

    Event lead, founding edition · 2025

    The Lisbon chapter of the international JunctionX hackathon series, bringing students, developers, researchers and companies together to build working prototypes for real challenges.

    How to Organize an Unforgettable Hackathon — on the blog
